`person:group-godrej` · flag: **clean** · confidence: verified · tickers: GODREJIND, GODREJCP, GODREJPROP, GODREJAGRO, ASTECLIFE

Flag: CLEAN. 127-year-old group; the family split amicably by a Family Settlement Agreement (30-Apr-2024, completed 18-Jul-2024): Adi and Nadir Godrej's side kept the listed Godrej Industries Group (Godrej Industries, Godrej Consumer Products, Godrej Properties, Godrej Agrovet, Astec Lifesciences); Jamshyd Godrej and Smita Godrej Crishna took unlisted Godrej & Boyce and the Vikhroli land bank, with a non-compete and brand-sharing arrangement. Promoters took 64.66% of Godrej Industries under the settlement. No promoter pledging; listed companies have not been used to fund family entities; succession was pre-announced (Pirojsha Godrej to succeed Nadir as GIG chair in Aug-2026). Points to watch: Godrej Industries is a holdco trading at a deep discount to its listed stakes; Godrej Properties raises equity often (QIPs) -- dilution, but at market prices; Astec Lifesciences losses. Lesson: a peaceful, pre-planned split with listed cos untouched is the good template versus litigated feuds (Ambani 2005, Birla-Lodha, TVS 2026). Status Nov-2026: no regulator orders found.

- **red flags:** holdco discount; frequent GPL equity raises
- **good conduct:** amicable 2024 split, no listed-entity value transfer

Sources:
- <https://businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/127-year-old-godrej-empire-splits-adi-nadir-to-keep-listed-firms-jamshyd-smita-get-unlisted-cos-land-bank-427735-2024-05-01>

body:
**False alarm with a ceiling: Asian Paints, Pidilite, Page at 40-60x for 15+ years** (`case_study:false-alarm-consumer-franchises-long-high-pe`, single-source). FLAG: 'too expensive' for two decades. Asian Paints trailing P/E median 50 (2005-26), Pidilite 52, Page mostly 40-80. CONTEXT: ROCE 26-42% (Asian Paints), 24-45% (Pidilite), 45-69% (Page) with low debt, dominant distribution and pricing power, so each rupee retained earned 25%+ and EPS compounded mid-to-high teens for 15+ years. Returns: Asian Paints Rs 39 (2005) -> Rs 3,576 (2022 peak), ~90x; Pidilite Rs 10.7 (2005) -> Rs 1,588 (Nov 2026), ~148x; Page Rs 272 (2007) -> Rs 53,453 (2022), ~197x. Buyers at 'fair' 40-50x did fine because the P/E held while EPS compounded. THE CEILING: when P/E reached ~2x its own long median (Asian Paints 117 and Pidilite ~100 in 2021; Page ~81 in 2022), subsequent 4-5-year returns were flat or negative even as EPS rose (Asian Paints Rs 2,776 Jan-2021 -> Rs 2,595 Nov-2026 while EPS rose ~54%; Pidilite +28% in 5 yrs on 2x EPS). Asian Paints also met a new deep-pocketed rival (Grasim's Birla Opus, 2024), a reminder that the moat itself is a variable. LESSON: a long high P/E is benign for high-ROCE franchises with long runways; the warning is not 'P/E > 40' but 'P/E far above the company's own history and growth slowing or competition entering'.

**False alarm: Info Edge's reported losses and 3% ROCE** (`case_study:false-alarm-info-edge-losses-low-roce`, verified). FLAGS: consolidated net losses in FY15 (-Rs 14 cr), FY17 (-43), FY20 (-246), FY23 (-70); ROCE 2-4% in most years; P/E swings from 16 to 565. CONTEXT: the consolidated numbers mix two things: (1) Naukri recruitment, a cash machine (standalone recruitment operating margin ~58-59% in Q4 FY26; debtor days 1-7; customers pay upfront, so deferred revenue funds the business), and (2) a venture portfolio (Zomato/Eternal from 2010, Policybazaar/PB Fintech, others) whose losses, impairments (e.g., Rs 276 cr 4B Networks write-off in Q3 FY23) and fair-value swings run through the P&L. The equity base is inflated by marked-up stakes, which crushes ROCE. FY22 PAT of Rs 12,882 cr was mostly a gain on Zomato. Sum-of-parts showed a profitable core plus listed stakes worth a large share of market cap. Stock: ~Rs 29 (2006) -> Rs 1,166 (Nov 2026), ~40x. LESSON: when consolidated losses come from investees or mark-to-market, re-cut the company by segment (standalone core margins + listed-stake value at market). Low ROCE caused by a big investment book is a capital-allocation question (are the bets good?), not an operating flaw.

A retailer has one unit (the store). A manufacturer has **three units that must not be mixed up**:
| Unit | What it measures | Where the data is |
|---|---|---|
| **Plant** (capacity × utilisation) | Physical output and fixed-cost absorption | Plant list `[AR26]`, BRSR "physical output" intensity, "70% utilisation" `[CC-Q4FY26]` |
| **Product line / node** (kVA band or engine platform: LHP, MHP, HD, HHP/QSK60/QSK95) | Price, mix and competition | Quarterly segment splits on calls; emission-norm categories |
| **Channel account** (GOEM, dealer, industrial OEM) | Who captures the margin; concentration | Ind AS 108 customer-concentration footnote; dealer counts |

body:
- **KEC: margins, debt and NWC.** These are near zero (10%, 18%, 11%), while the other two companies' medians are 70%, 79% and 69%. The cause is internal: legacy civil, metro and railway closures, JJM exposure, Saudi 20% retentions, and growth funded with debt. Every FY26 debt or NWC number was missed and then re-set.
- **KPIL: group P&L and balance-sheet guidance** (revenue 80%, debt 100%). Its guidance is conservative, volunteered and repeated. Misses are in subsidiaries (Fasttel write-off of INR 515 cr), asset-sale timing and capex discipline.
- **Skipper: capacity dates, segment targets and exports.** Group margin and finance cost were good (margin 70%).
- **Group revenue guidance** separates the three: KPIL 80%, Skipper 35%, KEC 16%.
